input_signals.name: Retained-Quality Debt Retirement
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(re, at)), 0), MUL(INDICATOR(SUB(dltr, dltis), 0), RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Net long-term debt retirement predicts higher returns when supported by a strong accumulated retained-earnings position.
input_signals.reasoning: High retained earnings identify firms whose debt reduction is more plausibly funded by durable internal value creation. The interaction separates disciplined balance-sheet improvement from debt retirement caused by asset sales, refinancing constraints, or contraction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_zscore( ratio( re, at ) ), 0 ), mul( indicator( sub( dltr, dltis ), 0 ), ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Persistent-Cash Payout Bottleneck
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms combining persistent operating cash profitability with large net shareholder payouts earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The minimum-rank construction requires both quality and payout strength, rather than allowing one theme to compensate for weakness in the other. High scores identify distributions that are more likely sustainable and informative about undervaluation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( add( prstkc, dvc ), sstk ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Stable Self-Funding Conjunction
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with stable operating cash generation and little reliance on net external financing earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Cash-flow stability makes financing restraint informative about genuine self-funding capacity rather than temporary underinvestment. The bottleneck interaction scores a firm highly only when both cash-flow reliability and external-financing discipline are present.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Quality Share-Count Alignment
input_signals.expression: SUB(MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)))), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))), IND_RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms combining persistent cash profitability with actual share-count contraction outperform firms combining weak cash profitability with dilution.
input_signals.reasoning: The two-sided corner construction creates economically distinct long and short portfolios rather than comparing selected repurchasers with a mass of zeros. Using realized share-count change also distinguishes repurchases that reduce dilution from announced or gross repurchase spending offset by employee issuance.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( growth( csho, 1 ) ) ) ), min( ind_rank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ), ind_rank( growth( csho, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Stable-Cash Dividend Commitment
input_signals.expression: MIN(MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))), MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(dvc, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(dvc, at), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Meaningful and stable dividends predict higher returns when supported by persistently strong and stable operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: The construction distinguishes credible dividend commitments from mechanically high but volatile aggregate payouts, a possible source of the prior payout signal’s weak portfolio evidence. Requiring a positive dividend level prevents nonpayers from scoring well merely because their dividend volatility is zero.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) ), min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( dvc, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( dvc, at ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Backed Effective Repurchase
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(prstkc, at)), IND_RANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Repurchases predict higher returns when supported by persistent operating cash flow and when gross repurchase spending produces an actual share-count contraction.
input_signals.reasoning: The expression explicitly requires cash quality, repurchase activity, and realized reduction in shares, preventing ordinary profitability growth or dilution from driving the signal independently. It also avoids unstable growth calculations involving gross profit near zero and distinguishes effective buybacks from repurchases offset by employee or acquisition-related issuance.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), min( ind_rank( ratio( prstkc, at ) ), ind_rank( neg( growth( csho, 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Maintenance-Cash Debt Stress
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(dltis, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Long-term debt issuance predicts lower returns when operating cash flow after depreciation is weak relative to industry peers.
input_signals.reasoning: Operating cash flow net of depreciation proxies recurring cash capacity after maintaining the productive asset base. Issuance intensity weights a centered quality measure, placing weak-capacity debt issuers in the adverse tail and strong-capacity issuers in the opposite tail instead of assuming debt issuance is favorable for all stable firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ), neg( ind_zscore( ma( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Post-Issuance Asset-Turnover Absorption
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(LAG(RATIO(sstk, at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Prior equity issuance is relatively favorable when followed by improving asset turnover and adverse when followed by deteriorating asset turnover.
input_signals.reasoning: Lagging issuance separates the financing decision from the subsequent operating evidence about how effectively the new capital was absorbed. Industry-standardized asset-turnover trends distinguish productive financing from dilution that expands the asset base without generating proportional sales.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( lag( ratio( sstk, at ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( trend( ratio( sale, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Trough Dilution Stress
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Share-count growth predicts lower returns when operating cash profitability is near the bottom of the firm’s own recent history.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a genuine non-compensatory interaction: the signal becomes large only when dilution coincides with a firm-specific cash-quality trough. Using the quality state’s own-history rank also changes the mechanism from the prior margin-plus-dilution composite and avoids the algebraic cancellation of complementary cross-sectional ranks.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( growth( csho, 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ts_rank( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquidity-Constrained Equity Preference
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at), 3))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(sstk, dltis), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms with weak working-capital liquidity, reliance on equity issuance rather than long-term debt predicts lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing leg measures the choice between equity and debt funding rather than gross equity issuance alone, while the liquidity rank determines how strongly that choice matters. This avoids dividing by a potentially small current ratio and interprets equity-heavy funding by illiquid firms as evidence of constrained debt capacity, adverse selection, or funding stress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( ma( ratio( sub( act, lct ), at ), 3 ) ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( sub( sstk, dltis ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Net-Debt Maintenance-Cash Stress
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Net long-term debt expansion predicts lower returns when recurring cash capacity after depreciation is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: Netting debt retirement from issuance distinguishes genuine balance-sheet expansion from refinancing transactions, a specific financing measurement issue in the prior strong signal. The signed quality conditioner creates adverse weak-capacity expanders and a favorable comparison group of strong-capacity expanders while preserving the maintenance-cash mechanism.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ) ), neg( ind_zscore( ma( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dividend-Weighted Residual Cash
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(dvc, at), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dvc), at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Meaningful dividend commitments predict higher returns when substantial operating cash remains after distributions and lower returns when dividends exhaust internal cash capacity.
input_signals.reasoning: Dividend intensity weights a signed measure of post-distribution cash capacity, directly contrasting sustainable and strained dividend payers rather than concentrating only mature payers in a compressed four-way bottleneck. Nonpayers receive little weight, while the short tail consists of firms maintaining dividends despite weak residual cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( dvc, at ), 3 ) ), ind_zscore( ma( ratio( sub( oancf, dvc ), at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Margin-Confirmed Financing Pivot
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(TREND(RATIO(ib, sale), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A shift from equity issuance toward repurchases predicts higher returns when accompanied by improving operating margins and lower returns when margins deteriorate.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing variable measures a change in capital-allocation regime rather than a static repurchase or issuance level. Weighting a signed margin trend by the strength of the financing pivot distinguishes operating recoveries that validate repurchases from defensive buybacks undertaken during weakening profitability.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( delta( ratio( sub( prstkc, sstk ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( trend( ratio( ib, sale ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Productive Deleveraging Validation
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at)), IND_ZSCORE(TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Net debt retirement predicts higher returns when accompanied by improving asset utilization and lower returns when it accompanies deteriorating asset utilization.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the equity-issuance absorption mechanism with a distinction between productive deleveraging and debt reduction caused by liquidation or operating contraction. Net retirement weights a signed, industry-standardized asset-turnover trend, creating opposing tails among deleveraging firms rather than making another timing adjustment to the archived issuance signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), at ) ), ind_zscore( trend( ratio( sale, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Weak-Cash Debt Rollover Stress
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(dltis, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dltr, at))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Heavy simultaneous debt issuance and retirement predict lower returns when maintenance-adjusted operating cash capacity is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: Jointly high issuance and retirement identify gross refinancing or rollover activity that disappears from net debt-flow measures. Weak recurring cash capacity makes such turnover more indicative of refinancing pressure, while the signed conditioner places well-supported rollovers in the opposite tail.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dltr, at ) ) ), neg( ind_zscore( ma( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Funded Dividend Strain
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(dltis, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dvc, at))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dvc), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Simultaneous debt issuance and dividend distributions predict lower returns when operating cash remaining after dividends is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing conjunction isolates firms that appear to borrow while maintaining shareholder distributions rather than ordinary debt issuers or dividend payers. A weak post-dividend cash position makes the policy more likely to reflect payout rigidity, agency problems, or an unsustainable effort to avoid a negative dividend signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dvc, at ) ) ), neg( ind_zscore( ma( ratio( sub( oancf, dvc ), at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Offset-Buyback Quality Trap
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(prstkc, at)), IND_RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Repurchase spending predicts lower returns when shares outstanding continue to grow and operating cash profitability is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing conjunction identifies ineffective buybacks that fail to offset employee, acquisition-related, or other equity issuance. Weak cash quality makes this mismatch more indicative of cosmetic payout policy or agency-driven compensation, rather than treating all repurchase spending as a favorable signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( prstkc, at ) ), ind_rank( growth( csho, 1 ) ) ), neg( ind_zscore( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Productivity-Confirmed Share Contraction
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))), IND_ZSCORE(TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Share-count contraction predicts higher returns when accompanied by improving asset utilization and lower returns when it occurs during deteriorating asset utilization.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the arithmetic blend of complementary debt-flow ranks with a single interaction between realized equity contraction and operating productivity. The signed asset-turnover trend distinguishes accretive share-base reduction from contraction associated with shrinking operations or distress, while common share-count data should preserve coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( growth( csho, 1 ) ) ), ind_zscore( trend( ratio( sale, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Productive Equity-Funded Deleveraging
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at))), IND_ZSCORE(TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity-financed debt reduction is relatively favorable when asset utilization improves and adverse when operating productivity deteriorates.
input_signals.reasoning: Simultaneous stock issuance and net debt retirement identify a financing substitution rather than ordinary external issuance or internally funded deleveraging. Improving turnover indicates that the recapitalization supports a viable operating base, whereas declining turnover suggests distressed dilution used primarily to satisfy creditors.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), at ) ) ), ind_zscore( trend( ratio( sale, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Quality Leveraged Repurchase
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(prstkc, at))), IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt-financed repurchases predict higher returns for firms with strong maintenance-adjusted cash capacity and lower returns for firms with weak cash capacity.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing conjunction specifically identifies repurchases accompanied by net debt expansion, distinguishing leveraged recapitalizations from internally funded buybacks. The signed cash-capacity conditioner separates credible undervaluation-driven leverage from repurchases that increase financial risk despite weak recurring resources.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( prstkc, at ) ) ), ind_zscore( ma( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Weak-Cash Payout Substitution
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvc), at), 1)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A shift from dividends toward repurchases predicts lower returns when operating cash profitability is weak and relatively favorable returns when cash profitability is strong.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing action is a change in payout composition, not another ineffective-buyback or payout-level measure. Moving toward discretionary repurchases while cash quality is weak may reveal reluctance to sustain a dividend commitment, whereas strong cash generation makes the same flexibility less concerning.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( delta( ratio( sub( prstkc, dvc ), at ), 1 ) ), neg( ind_zscore( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Supported Equity Deleveraging
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at))), IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity-funded debt reduction predicts higher returns when supported by strong recurring cash capacity and lower returns when undertaken by weak-cash firms.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests whether the successful recapitalization mechanism depends on operating cash viability rather than the repeatedly used asset-turnover trend. The signed maintenance-cash conditioner separates proactive balance-sheet optimization from distressed equity issuance used to appease creditors.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), at ) ) ), ind_zscore( ma( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Explicit Weak-Cash Payout Switch
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(prstkc, at), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(dvc, at), 1)))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Increasing repurchases while reducing dividends predicts lower returns when operating cash profitability is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: Requiring both sides of the payout switch distinguishes a deliberate move from committed dividends toward discretionary repurchases from a noisy change in their net difference. Weak cash quality makes the switch more indicative of payout fragility or an attempt to preserve flexibility without formally eliminating distributions.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( delta( ratio( prstkc, at ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( dvc, at ), 1 ) ) ) ), neg( ind_zscore( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Net-Borrowed Dividend Strain
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dvc, at))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dvc), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Dividend distributions accompanied by net debt expansion predict lower returns when post-dividend operating cash is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: Netting debt retirement removes refinancing activity and isolates genuine balance-sheet expansion used alongside distributions. This measurement change should sharpen the distinction between debt-supported payout strain and firms that issue and retire debt concurrently without increasing leverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dvc, at ) ) ), neg( ind_zscore( ma( ratio( sub( oancf, dvc ), at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Equity-Funded Dividend Strain
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dvc, at))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dvc), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Simultaneous equity issuance and dividend payments predict lower returns when operating cash remaining after distributions is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal identifies firms that dilute shareholders while preserving a dividend despite inadequate internal funding. It provides a direct financing-source comparison with debt-funded dividend strain, testing whether the adverse mechanism is generic payout support or specifically borrowing-driven.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dvc, at ) ) ), neg( ind_zscore( ma( ratio( sub( oancf, dvc ), at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Quality Leveraged Share Retirement
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)))), IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt-financed share-count contraction predicts higher returns when recurring cash capacity is strong and lower returns when cash capacity is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: Actual share-count contraction verifies that increased leverage produces a realized reduction in outside claims rather than repurchase spending offset by new issuance. The design isolates whether the prior leveraged-repurchase evidence is stronger when financing effectiveness is measured by the balance-sheet outcome.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( growth( csho, 1 ) ) ) ), ind_zscore( ma( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Weak-Cash Equity Churn
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(prstkc, at))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))

input_signals.reasoning: Concurrent issuance and repurchase identify equity churn that may arise from compensation dilution, acquisition issuance, or inefficient treasury activity rather than a directional capital-allocation decision. Weak cash quality makes this costly round trip more indicative of agency problems or external funding dependence.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( prstkc, at ) ) ), neg( ind_zscore( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.hypothesis: Simultaneous dividend retrenchment and share-count dilution predict lower returns when operating cash profitability is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: A dividend reduction and dilution are two distinct financing confirmations that internal and external funding conditions have deteriorated. input_signals.name: Cash-Backed Net Payout Expansion
